newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi bank sees lower 1997 average Brent price.
newsitem.headline: Saudi bank sees lower 1997 average Brent price.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's National Commercial Bank (NCB) expects North Sea Brent crude to average $20 a barrel in 1997, 70 cents below last year's average.

"Our forecast for average Brent crude prices this year is $20 a barrel, which is 3.4 percent below last year's average of $20.70 a barrel," NCB chief economist Henry Azzam said in the bank's latest monthly report.
Robust world oil demand was also pushing oil prices to higher sustainable levels, according to NCB.

"The sustainable crude oil price range having languished in the bracket of $15-20 per barrel for the past 10 years or so has now moved up by $3 a barrel to the $18-23 a barrel," said the report describing Saudi Arabia's economic outlook for 1997.
NCB agreed with a forecast by the Paris-based International Energy Agency (IEA) pointing to a 1.9 million barrels per day (bpd) increase in world petroleum demand this year to 73.6 million bpd.
In contrast to the IEA, the bank expects the call on OPEC oil to rise by 700,000 bpd to 26.2 million bpd in 1997 because of a less than expected surge in non-OPEC supply growth.
"We view the IEA projection for non-OPEC supply as grossly exaggerated," NCB reported.
